source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.23
text: Recommended transplanting method for seed-production fields: (1) Pull seedlings when they are 18–20 days old. (2) Mark straight planting lines using a string with markers spaced 20 cm apart, and transplant in straight rows so plants can later be inspected/rogued easily. (3) Transplant a single seedling per hill (not a clump), at a planting depth of about 2–3 cm into the soil. A companion planting-grid diagram shows a spacing pattern of about 20 cm between hills within a row and about 25 cm between rows (a 20 cm × 25 cm grid). (5) Maintain a shallow water depth of about 3–5 cm in the days immediately after transplanting. (6) Within 1–2 weeks after transplanting, replant/fill any hills that failed to establish, and separate out any seedlings that clumped together during transplanting.
